trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Two candidates, both in the false-positive classes. "The refactor identifies this directly in the spectral sequence, rather than via shell-model fitting" is a substantive methodological contrast. "It is not the Plancherel-weighted character sum ... which vanishes identically at certain atomic-braid cycle types" is load-bearing disambiguation between two genuinely different objects, and the whole "Operator-level support" section exists to make that distinction.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: No change. Separate one-voice note: "The refactor identifies this" leaks the editing process into scholarly prose - "refactor" is not a mathematical object. Proposed: "The spectral sequence identifies this directly, rather than via shell-model fitting."

trap-triples.evidence: The Discussion's three numbered evidence items are distinct in kind (numerical, conditional-equivalence, phenomenological); a genuine enumeration.

trap-closing-aphorism.evidence: Closes on a scope statement about the downstream cone, not a quotable line - and an honest one ("stays conjectural until either the conjecture is proved or the prediction is demoted").

trap-meta-commentary.evidence: "This conditional structure justifies authoring both conjectures together." The sentence narrates the document's own construction - why two blocks were written as a pair - rather than stating mathematics. The mathematical content it is standing in for is the next sentence ("A proof of either implies the other under the substrate axioms").
trap-meta-commentary.notes: STRUCTURAL (deleting it changes the paragraph's opening and the following "The categorical conjecture ... the homological conjecture ..." depends on the pairing being introduced), not edited. Proposed: open the paragraph with the content instead - "Under the substrate axioms the two conjectures are equivalent: the categorical one is the Hecke-side content, the homological one its brane-tower-side image under Yekutieli rigidity" - and drop the authoring sentence entirely.

trap-thesis-restatement.evidence: Each section closes on new content.

trap-superlative.evidence: Discussion item 3: "the seven values {2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126} form the only nucleon counts at which the experimental binding curve exhibits a discontinuous first-derivative drop". "The only" is unqualified and overstated - the sub-magic numbers (6, 14, 16, 28-region N=32/34) show observed kinks in separation energies, and 126 is established as magic for neutrons only. The phrase "discontinuous first-derivative drop" is also loose for a curve defined on integers.
trap-superlative.notes: STRUCTURAL / math-adjacent, not edited. Proposed: "the seven values ... are the nucleon counts at which the experimental separation-energy curve shows the largest drops". Two further items for the coordinating session: (1) the biconditional "A proof of either implies the other under the substrate axioms" is stronger than the argument given, which runs one way only (categorical neutrality -> self-dual BB stratification -> the E_infty vanishing); Discussion item 2 repeats it as "Conditional equivalence". (2) An evidence gap: the block says verification confirms E_infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 "at n = 2, 8, 20" and that the downstream cone affects "n in {50, 82, 126}" - n = 28 is in neither list, so its status is unstated.
